name: NUMISHEET '93 two-dimensional draw bending, mild steel
status: future independent benchmark target; not reproduced by the current solver

canonical_numisheet93_b3.source: Makinouchi et al., NUMISHEET '93 benchmark B3; reproduced in Burchitz, Improvement of Springback Prediction in Sheet Forming Simulation, Appendix A.3
canonical_numisheet93_b3.force_stroke_data: A same-condition B3 punch-force versus stroke curve has not been identified in the cited accessible sources. Burchitz Fig. 3.7 is a different top-hat mesh study (85 mm stroke, friction coefficient 0.162) and must not be used as B3 data. Flores et al. Fig. 21 is for the following square-sheet deep-drawing example, not the B3 strip test.
canonical_numisheet93_b3.scope_note: This canonical B3 case is distinct from the Abaqus input-deck variant below, which uses a 2.45 kN holder load. The current plane-strain J2 frictionless run matches neither case fully.

reference_run.variant: mild steel with 2.45 kN blank-holder force
reference_run.force_stroke_history: The official input deck requests RF and U history output at the punch reference node; an output database is not included in this repository.

material.hardening_data: Tabulated yield stress versus equivalent plastic strain from the official reference input deck; values are stored below in MPa.

process.tools: rigid analytical die, punch, and blank holder
process.springback: remove tool contact and solve a static equilibrium step

analytical_tool_profiles_from_reference_.profile_point_convention: raw START, LINE, and CIRCL data-line coordinates from the input deck; CIRCL stores endpoint then center
analytical_tool_profiles_from_reference_.coordinate_transform_note: These are source-deck analytical surface coordinates and reference-node coordinates. Apply the Abaqus cylindrical-surface local frame and rigid-body transform before comparing them to blank mesh coordinates.

published_comparison.source: M. Puso, A Users Manual for the Nonlinear Kinematic Hardening Model for Cyclic Loading, UCRL-MA-140587, 2000, Table 2
published_comparison.comparison_note: The published isotropic-hardening simulation uses a fitted power-law material curve, not the tabular hardening data in the official Abaqus input deck stored above. Treat 17.1 deg as the experimental target; 17.20 deg is a method-level comparison, not a same-material reference run.

related_experimental_springback_validati.source: T. Da Silva Botelho, E. Bayraktar, G. Inglebert, Comparison of experimental and simulation results of 2D-draw-bend springback, Journal of Achievements in Materials and Manufacturing Engineering 18(1-2), 2006, pp. 275-278
related_experimental_springback_validati.material_model: The paper's FEA assumes material isotropy with nonlinear strain hardening. The exact stress-strain curve transcription should be checked against the source table before quantitative replication; the isotropic assumption differs from canonical Hill48 B3.

springback_measurement_definitions.theta1: angle between Ox and segment AB
springback_measurement_definitions.theta2: angle between segments AB and EF

related_experimental_springback_validati.scope_note: Use as a related experimental/FEA springback validation case, not as the canonical Numisheet B3 dataset or as force-stroke/thickness data. The paper's isotropic material assumption, angle convention, and contact split (frictionless punch, Coulomb friction at die and holder) differ from the Hill48 B3 and 17.1-degree flange-angle targets above.

available_in_source: 2D plane-strain finite-strain J2 and Hill48 material updates with consistent tangents
transactional plastic history updates for Newton trial states
rigid punch, die, and blank-holder contact with frictionless and Coulomb options
forming, tool removal, springback, and optional reference-curve comparison outputs
benchmark_gaps: a converged and documented full 70 mm path for the exact reference conditions
the reference shell formulation with five through-thickness integration points, or a demonstrated solid-to-shell equivalence
an independent punch reaction-force versus stroke dataset for same-condition error measurement

a springback comparison using the exact canonical Hill48 and tabulated material law: Puso's 17.20-degree result uses a fitted power law; a related 2006 mild-steel experiment at 19.6 kN is now recorded separately, but exact constitutive equivalence has not been established
implementation_status.scope_note: Source availability does not establish numerical validation. The current finite-strain solid contact driver remains experimental until the full path and reference comparisons are reproduced.

puso_isotropic_hardening.source: M. Puso, A Users Manual for the Nonlinear Kinematic Hardening Model for Cyclic Loading, UCRL-MA-140587, 2000, Table 1
puso_isotropic_hardening.law: sigma_y(p) = sigma_y0 + sum_i Q_i * (1 - exp(-b_i * p))
puso_isotropic_hardening.scope_note: This published isotropic law is a distinct material comparison path; it does not replace the official Abaqus deck hardening curve above.
